newsitem.title: GEORGIA: IMF set to examine Georgia 1997 spending plans.
newsitem.headline: IMF set to examine Georgia 1997 spending plans.

text.p: A International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation is due to arrive in the Georgian capital Tbilisi on Thursday for talks on further help for the former Soviet republic and to look at the 1997 budget.
The assessment will determine the fate of a second tranche of a $80 million IMF loan.
Hunter Monroe, IMF representative in Georgia, said last week that continued lending depended on a favorable evaluation of the budget and other aspects of Georgia's economic reform programme.
Georgia depends heavily on IMF funding to close a planned 200 million lari ($155 million) 1997 budget deficit and analysts say currency stability could be at risk without the money.
Georgia has brought inflation below one percent per month and the lari has held steady at around 1.3 to the dollar since the currency was introduced in 1995.
The planned 1997 budget deficit is 50 percent lower than in 1996, but the IMF wants Georgia to improve tax collection.
Georgia, a mountainous country of five million between Turkey and Russia, was an outpost of relative prosperity in Soviet times when it enjoyed big subsidies from Moscow.
But it was left to fend for itself when the superpower collapsed. Civil and ethnic conflict have made it one of the poorest republics in the Commonwealth of Independent States. ($1 =1.29 lari)
